name: Synthetic mortality table and survival engine
description: The deterministic heart of the demo: a generated synthetic mortality table for ages 0 to 120 (male and female) and a pure survival engine. Every story below is fully specified; implement exactly what it says, nothing more. Formula for x >= 1: q(x) = min(1, A + B * exp(C * x)). Male A=0.0002 B=0.00003 C=0.095. Female A=0.0002 B=0.00002 C=0.095. Age 0 is fixed: male 0.004, female 0.0035. Age 120 is fixed at 1 for both.

userStories.title: Generate data/mortality.csv
userStories.description: Create tools/generate-table.mjs. It writes data/mortality.csv (create the data/ folder if missing). Line 1 is exactly: # SYNTHETIC illustrative mortality. Not for real actuarial use. Line 2 is the header: age,qx_male,qx_female. Then one row per age 0..120 with rates printed using toFixed(8). Use the constants from the PRD description. Put the formula and constants in a comment at the top of the file. Use Math.exp only; no Math.random.
acceptanceCriteria: node tools/generate-table.mjs exits 0 and data/mortality.csv has exactly 123 lines (comment, header, 121 rows)
Row for age 80 male is 0.06015 to 5 decimal places (0.0002 + 0.00003 * exp(7.6) = 0.0601459)
Running the generator twice gives byte-identical output (check with cmp)
For both sexes q(x) <= q(x+1) for every x from 1 to 119

userStories.title: Table loader src/engine/table.mjs
userStories.description: Create src/engine/table.mjs exporting parseTable(csvText). Skip lines starting with # and the header line. Return { male: Float64Array or number[] of length 121, female: same } indexed by age. Throw new Error(`Missing age ${x}`) if any age 0..120 is absent, Error(`Duplicate age ${x}`) if repeated, and Error(`Rate out of range at age ${x}`) if any rate is < 0 or > 1. No DOM, no fetch, no fs inside this module; it takes the CSV text as a string.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/table.test.mjs loads data/mortality.csv with fs, calls parseTable, and asserts both arrays have length 121 and male[0] === 0.004
A CSV with age 50 removed throws an Error whose message contains 'Missing age 50'
A CSV where age 10 male is 1.2 throws an Error whose message contains 'age 10'
node --test tests/ passes

userStories.title: Survival engine src/engine/survival.mjs
userStories.description: Create src/engine/survival.mjs exporting two pure functions. survivors(cohort, qx, startAge) returns a plain array lx where lx[0] === cohort is the count at startAge, lx[i+1] = lx[i] * (1 - qx[startAge + i]) for ages up to 120, and the final element (for age 121) is 0 because q(120) is 1. Its length is 121 - startAge + 1. No rounding anywhere. applyImprovement(qx, pct) returns a NEW array where every element is (1 - pct) * qx[x]; it throws Error('pct must be between 0 and 0.3') otherwise. Put a comment at the top: terminal age convention, everyone alive at 120 dies in that year.
acceptanceCriteria: survivors(1000000, male, 0)[0] === 1000000, its length is 122, and its last element is 0
survivors(1000000, male, 60).length === 62
For every i, lx[i+1] <= lx[i] (never increases)

survivors(1000, new Array(121).fill(0), 0) is all 1000 except the last element, which is 0 only if q(120) is forced to 1: so test with a copy of the table where q(120)=1 and all other q=0 and assert lx is 1000 up to age 120 and 0 at 121
With q(30)=1 in a copy of the table, survivors from age 0 is 0 from index 31 onwards
applyImprovement(male, 0.1)[80] is within 1e-12 of 0.9 * male[80]; survivors with improved rates are >= baseline at every index
applyImprovement(male, 0.31) and applyImprovement(male, -0.01) both throw
All of the above live in tests/survival.test.mjs and node --test tests/ passes

userStories.title: Independent reference check tools/reference.py and tests/reference.test.mjs
userStories.description: Create tools/reference.py (Python 3, standard library only). It reads data/mortality.csv, skips # and header lines, and for each sex computes l(0)=1000000, l(x+1)=l(x)*(1-q(x)) with plain floats. It writes data/reference.json as {"male": {"30": ..., "65": ..., "90": ..., "110": ...}, "female": {...}} with unrounded floats. Do not import or read any JavaScript. Then create tests/reference.test.mjs which reads data/reference.json, runs survivors(1000000, qx, 0) from the JS engine, and asserts Math.abs(js[age] - ref[age]) < 0.5 for all eight values.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 tools/reference.py exits 0 and data/reference.json has exactly eight numbers
Male 30 is above 990000 and male 110 is below 1000 (sanity bounds, not exact values)
tests/reference.test.mjs passes under node --test tests/
Nothing in data/reference.json or tools/reference.py is edited after the Python script first writes it; if the JS disagrees, fix the JS

technicalNotes.rationale: Every story is specified to the line. Numbers are the deliverable.
